st: Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they break down.
Add the spinach and salt a handful at a time. Cook for 5 minutes, then keep warm.
Bring [[3 cups]] water and the salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] cornmeal with [[1 cup]] cold water to make a smooth slurry. Whisk it into the boiling water.
Cook for 3 minutes, whisking, until thick like porridge.
Lower the heat and add the remaining cornmeal a handful at a time, stirring hard with a wooden spoon.
Cook and stir for 5 minutes until the ugali is stiff and pulls away from the pot.
Shape into a mound with the spoon and serve with the greens.

ing: goat meat or beef short ribs
st: Cut the meat into large chunks. Rub with the lemon juice, garlic, pepper flakes, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and oil.
Marinate in the fridge for at least [[1 hour]].
Heat a charcoal grill, or oven to 350°F (175°C).
Grill the meat over medium-low heat, turning often, for about 1 hour 15 minutes, until tender and browned.
Check that the thickest piece reaches 160°F (71°C) for beef, or 165°F (74°C) for goat.
Mix the onion, tomatoes, cilantro and [[0.5 tsp]] salt into a quick kachumbari.
Rest the meat for 10 minutes. Chop it into pieces and serve with the kachumbari.
Cut the potatoes into thin fries. Pat dry with a towel.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the potatoes for 6 to 8 minutes until golden. Drain on paper towels.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper. Stir in the onion and tomato.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Add the fries and spread them out, then pour the egg mixture over.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until set on the bottom. Flip using a plate and cook 2 minutes more.
Slide onto a plate and serve with ketchup.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Cook the onions for 12 minutes until deep golden brown.
Add the beef and brown for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns and salt. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in [[2 cups]] hot water, cover, and simmer for 40 minutes until the beef is tender.
Wash the rice until the water runs mostly clear, and drain well.
Add the rice and [[3 cups]] hot water, making sure it covers the rice by about half an inch.
Bring to a boil, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes.
Rest off the heat for 10 minutes, then fluff gently and serve.
Soak 8 wooden skewers in water for [[30 minutes]] so they do not burn.
Mix the garlic, ginger, lemon juice, chili flakes, curry powder, oil and salt in a bowl.
Add the beef cubes and stir until coated. Marinate for [[1 hour]] in the fridge.
Thread the beef and onion chunks onto the skewers.
Heat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat.
Cook the skewers for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and the beef reaches 145°F (63°C) or more.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.
Oil your knife and hands before peeling the green bananas, since they stain. Soak the chunks in cold water.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and beef and brown for 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, turmeric and salt. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the water, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes until the beef is nearly tender.
Drain the bananas and add them to the pot with the coconut milk.
Simmer, covered, for 20 minutes more until the bananas are soft and the sauce is thick.
Stir gently and serve warm.
Mix the flour and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Add the water and knead for 5 minutes until soft. Rub with [[2 tbsp]] oil and rest for [[30 minutes]].
Cook the beef, half the onion, the bell pepper, curry powder and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a pan for 8 minutes, until no pink remains. Cool slightly.
Divide the dough into 4 balls. Stretch each into a very thin square on an oiled counter.
Spoon the filling on the center. Crack an egg on top, and sprinkle on the cheese.
Fold the four sides over to make a square parcel.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil on a flat griddle over medium heat.
Cook the parcel 3 minutes per side until golden and the egg is set. Repeat with the others.
Slice each parcel in half and serve hot.

ing: such as snapper, cut in pieces
st: Season the fish with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and half the lime juice.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and curry powder and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until broken down and saucy.
Pour in the coconut milk, add the chili if using, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the fish and spoon sauce over. Simmer gently for 8 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Finish with the remaining lime juice, salt and cilantro. Serve with rice or chapati.
Heat the oil in a pot. Cook the onion for 4 minutes, then add the tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the potatoes, turmeric, cumin, salt, chili and water. Bring to a boil.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes are very soft.
Mash about a third of the potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Stir in the lemon juice and tamarind, and simmer 5 minutes more. Taste for tangy balance.
Pour the soup into bowls and add the bhajia fritters.
Top with the diced mango and cilantro. Serve hot.
Mix the flour, salt and sugar in a bowl.
Add [[2 tbsp]] oil and the warm water slowly, mixing until a dough forms. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and soft.
Cover and rest for [[30 minutes]].
Divide into 8 balls. Roll one into a thin 8-inch round.
Brush with melted butter, roll into a rope, then coil into a spiral. Repeat with all balls and rest 10 minutes.
Roll each coil flat again into a thin 7-inch round.
Heat a skillet over medium heat. Cook the chapati for 1 minute, flip, brush with oil, cook 1 minute, then flip again.
Cook until golden with brown spots, about 3 minutes total. Stack and cover to keep soft.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, cardamom and salt.
Beat the egg with the warm coconut milk and [[1 tbsp]] oil. Add to the dry ingredients.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise for [[1 hour]].
Roll the dough about half an inch thick. Cut into triangles.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 340°F (170°C).
Fry the mandazi 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and puffed.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
Rinse the rice in cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Drain.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes.
Add the cardamom and rice. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk, water and salt. Stir well.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat to the lowest setting and cover tightly.
Cook for 18 minutes without lifting the lid.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Grease a baking sheet or shallow dish with oil. Have a rolling pin or spatula and a sharp knife ready, because the candy sets fast.
Toast the grated coconut in a dry wide pan over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, stirring often, until lightly golden. Move it to a bowl.
Add [[1 cup]] sugar and [[0.25 cup]] water to the same pan. Cook over medium heat, stirring, until the sugar melts and turns a light amber, about 6 minutes.
Quickly stir in the toasted coconut, [[1 tsp]] cardamom and the peanuts. Mix for 1 minute until everything is coated. Take care, the syrup is extremely hot.
Scrape onto the greased sheet and press flat to 0.5 inch thick with an oiled spatula or rolling pin.
Let it cool 5 minutes, then cut into diamonds or squares while still warm. Cool fully before lifting out.
nt: Pan toasted, then set in caramelized sugar
Best swap: brown sugar for white sugar, same amount, for a deeper flavor. Skip the peanuts if allergic, and use sesame seeds.
